Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY July 12, 2007 MR. MARVIN M. ARBOLEDA Provincial Political Officer KGMA Foundation; Inc. Romblon Chapter Romblon, Romblon Dear Mr. Arboleaa: This is a rejoinder to your letter dated 24 May 2007 wherein you inquired wnat are the allowable expenditures and appropriations for tne Office of Senior Citizen Affairs (OSCA for brevity) pursuant to Section 13 of RA 9257. Section 13 of RA 9257 provides: "SEC. 13. Appropriations. The necessary appropriaüon for the operation and maintenance of the OSCA sha// be appropriated and approved by the /oca/ government units concerned. The amount necessary to carry out the provisions of this Act upon its effectivity sha// be charged out of the furtds of the Office Of the President. Thereafter, any such sum as sha// be needed for the regular implementation of this Act sha// be included in subsequent Genera/ Appropr;aDons Act fo//ovving its enactment inio law. The first sentence of the cited provision answers the question as to what entity shah provide for the maintenance and operating expenses Of the OSCA. Per COA Circular 2003-01 dated June 17, 2003 maintenance and operating expenses include but is not limited to the following items: Traveling, supplies and materials, utility, communication, professional services, etc. Hence, applying the said COA circular, expenses for traveling, supplies and materials, utility, communication, professional services , etc. snall be the responsibility of LGU. Note however, that salaries and wages are not included as expensditures falling under MOOE per the above cited COA Circular as they belong to other categories of expenses otherwise known as Personal Services.

However, this level is of the view that expenses for salaries and wages may still oe given to the head and personnel of the OSCA thru an ordinance craftea by tne LGU for that purpose in as much as RA 9257 is silent on this issue. Stated othervvise, since an ordinance for that purpose is not prohibitea under said law permissibility of such an ordinance is preferred otherwise we will have an instance where a law expressly allows Maintenance and Operating Expenses while disallowing expenses for Personal Services. This is absurd interpretation and should be avoided. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, PASCU ERON UZ, JR. istant Head Executive A DIR. ROLANDO l.
